targets[].ip/port are caller-controlled and passed to ping_ip_and_port, which runs subprocess.run with a fixed argv list (never shell=True) and a socket connect_ex; the ip value used in the subprocess call is either a syntactically valid dotted-quad (passed socket.inet_aton) or a getaddrinfo-resolved numeric address, so no argument/command injection is possible, and probing arbitrary attacker-given IP/port pairs is exactly this tool's declared purpose (a network diagnostics tool), matching the anti-false-positive rule for tools whose whole job is to act on a caller-given address with no further twist.
